html:
Proxmox VE skill and API

For setup and everyday requests, start with Using Proxmox VE. This page describes the implementation, session state and generated API contract.

Proxmox is an optional native skill and is disabled by default. Enable/add proxmox in the existing capability selection for the applicable prompt, conversation, or global settings. Installing this release does not add it to default selections, including upgrades of legacy opt-out selections.

In Parameter Store, select Proxmox Server beside New, then click New. This prefills the existing Value JSON editor; fill in the server and password and save normally:

{
  "profile_type": "server_connection",
  "profile_version": 1,
  "service": "proxmox",
  "scheme": "https",
  "server": "pve.home.example",
  "port": 8006,
  "username": "root@pam",
  "password": "<your password>",
  "verify_tls": true
}

Save it as home_proxmox, then ask:

From @home_proxmox, turn on windows11.

A typed reference makes the four entry tools initially available only if capability policy already allows them. The reference grants no approval, Gateway access, or additional capability. Ordinary requests use:

Tool Behavior
proxmox.server_info Read version and nodes; publish verified server context.
proxmox.guest_list List QEMU VMs and LXC containers across the cluster.
proxmox.guest_status Resolve an exact name/VMID and obtain fresh status.
proxmox.guest_power Resolve, check state, apply power action, wait for task, verify.

server_ref is optional with one accepted/current verified server. Multiple servers require an explicit accepted key. Guest resolution uses exact numeric VMID, then exact name, then a unique case-insensitive exact name; no fuzzy or substring matching can select a guest for mutation. Node and QEMU/LXC routing are internal. “Turn off” means shutdown. stop means explicitly requested hard power-off. Failed shutdown never escalates to stop. Start/shutdown/stop and other target-state actions return changed=false when the target state already holds; reboot/reset are not reduced to a running-state no-op. Supported actions are checked against the pinned guest-type endpoint inventory.

Power tools default to wait=true, timeout_seconds=120 (1–3600). UPID polling is bounded runtime work with cancellation, not model polling. wait=false returns a pending task, without claiming final state. Task failures/timeouts preserve the UPID. Cancellation stops local waiting; it does not claim to cancel the remote task. Uncertain mutations are never automatically replayed; the power helper attempts a fresh state reconciliation and reports unknown effect.

Authentication and session state

The runtime translates the accepted typed profile into a literal HTTP v3 session_login profile. Gateway HTTP performs POST /api2/json/access/ticket, extracts PVEAuthCookie, and supplies CSRFPreventionToken for writes. The model never calls login, builds headers, or constructs REST paths for domain tools.

Sessions are scoped to conversation, Gateway route/identity, parameter key and revision, origin, and a digest of the effective authentication values. They survive individual run cleanup. A warm conversation reuses its ticket; Gateway expiry or a bounded read-side 401 renews it silently. Detectably expired sessions renew before dispatching writes. Profile updates/deletes invalidate known sessions immediately; accepting a new revision also retires the old known scope. Conversation delete/abandon invalidates sessions and releases its runtime authentication state. Requests without a conversation use the existing per-run authentication lifetime.

All entry and model-exposed generated tools accept optional auth_values containing only literal username/password strings. The runtime validates a detached overlay; unknown fields and structural changes are rejected before dispatch. Values preserve exact whitespace and never update Parameter Store. Saved and transient passwords use the same session provider. Missing values return credential_required, exact missing_fields, and executed=false. The Agent asks for all missing values in one ordinary ask_user reply, then retries with auth_values on its next normal turn. Authentication rejection is reported separately and can be retried with replacement values. Accepted literal parameter snapshots survive restart. Legacy opaque handles require the exact historical store revision.

Parameter Store and accepted checkpoints retain literal profiles. PARAMETERS controls their consumer projections. Typed values can be exported through the parameter environment; see Redaction.

HTTPS verification defaults on. verify_tls=false explicitly selects the existing insecure TLS mode for installations with self-signed certificates. No TLS failure retries insecurely. IPv4, IPv6, and hostnames are supported. Gateway identity verification remains authoritative, independently of target TLS.

Verified Working Context retains configured server identity and revision/provenance, including the configured account. It never stores transient usernames/passwords or the effective authentication recipe. WORKING_CONTEXT optionally projects its consumer copy. Guest status still comes from fresh receipts.

API sections and generated tools

The shipped 9.2 API inventory contains 680 method/path descriptors, including 678 model-exposed operations and two internal /access/ticket operations. All raw tools share the same executor/session transport as the entry tools.

discover_tools(skill_ids=["proxmox"]) exposes only entry tools and root section metadata. discover_tools(section_ids=["proxmox.nodes.node.qemu.vmid.status"]) exposes that section's directly owned tools and child section metadata. Discovery is non-recursive. Discover .status.start to obtain the start endpoint schema. Discovering a new Proxmox slice replaces its previously advertised raw slice, while retaining entry tools; repeated exploration cannot accumulate the entire API. Exact tool discovery remains available within the capability envelope.

Raw arguments contain parameters (vendor named path/query/body parameters), optional server_ref, auth_values, wait, and timeout_seconds. auth_values is a wrapper argument and never enters PVE parameters or request bodies. Paths are percent-encoded; reads and DELETE use query fields, POST/PUT use URL-encoded forms. Booleans are sent as 0/1 and arrays as repeated fields. Writes use normal effect/approval policy. Uploads additionally accept a granted upload_context_id and reuse Gateway multipart/file transport. Download-capable operations accept response_mode="artifact" to retain a response as an existing Context artifact. Existing HTTP body, response, and upload bounds apply (2 MiB inline response, 8 MiB file transfer); this is not a bulk ISO streaming transport or interactive WebSocket console. Literal authentication reaches execution unchanged. Optional central redaction affects only consumer projections.

Updating the pinned API

Canonical source: the official Proxmox API Viewer apidoc.js JSON literal. The vendored gzip retains the exact downloaded bytes; the generator parses JSON and never executes downloaded JavaScript. Runtime loads generated files offline and never fetches vendor documentation.

The source manifest records SHA-256, source URL, fetch date, generator version, target release, counts, and version evidence. The current snapshot is associated with the co-published official documentation version 9.2.12, built September 18, 2026. The API Viewer itself contains no embedded package/git revision; this limitation is recorded instead of inventing a commit identity. Do not relabel an arbitrary old/community pve-api.json as a current release.

To update, retrieve the official viewer asset and the version marker from the co-published administration guide, review the target release, and update skills/proxmox/vendor/apidoc.js.gz and vendor/source.json with the exact uncompressed source digest. Compress with gzip.compress(data, mtime=0). Then run:

.venv/bin/python scripts/generate_proxmox_api.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/generate_proxmox_api.py --check
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_proxmox_skill.py

The generator rejects mismatched source hashes/version evidence, reports removed method/path identities, and produces deterministic descriptors, sections, and a manifest. Tests independently enumerate every source method, check ID uniqueness and validity, validate schemas, and compare generated bytes. IDs depend on method/path, with deterministic hashes for ambiguous normalization/long names. PVE property-string formats remain strings; source schemas are retained for review. Perl-only patterns and variant constraints dependent on server-side existing state remain server-validated. No endpoint method is silently dropped.

Generated files are smTO-owned build output. The vendor artifact remains upstream API reference material; it is never model prompt content.
